LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity. The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves. But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December. How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis It is hard not to pick the Jaguars here, and they once again get a clean sweep. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team. The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore. Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud. The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense. The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years. According to NextGenStats, Jacksonville has generated a 39.6% pressure rate this season (8th-highest), and its pressures have arrived in 2.43 seconds on average, the quickest in the NFL. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most. This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. home.blurb: On Thursday night, the Baltimore Ravens played their first full game since losing star quarterback Lamar Jackson to a significant thumb injury. It remains unclear when or if the two-time MVP will be able to return this season. DeCosta and Co. could look to get out of Jackson's contract rather than restructuring and extending it. There's no guarantee they will, of course, but many in the media have raised the prospect this week. The fact that Jackson didn't sign an extension this past offseason plays a role in the mounting speculation about his future. Under his current deal, he can't receive the franchise tag and cannot be traded without his permission. Jackson can, if he wants, play out his contract and be an unrestricted free agent in 2028. Given the massive cap hit he's set to hold next year, though, the Ravens might consider making him available before then. They could, in theory, release him with a post-June 1 designation and save $52 million in 2027 cap space. "Anytime a special player is available, which he is, you've got to do the work," Ballard said, per ESPN's Stephen Holder . If Jackson becomes available in the offseason, Indianapolis may do the work again. It would likely have to trade future draft capital, since it sent its 2027 first-rounder to the Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade. However, without a first-round pick, the Colts may also have to weigh non-draft options at quarterback more heavily. The Atlanta Falcons should probably be viewed as a bit of a wild card right now. Atlanta is rolling with 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. While the jury is still out on the young signal-caller, the Falcons seem to believe in him. If Atlanta could swing a deal for Jackson, it could extend him and still have money left over to flesh out its roster. The Falcons are projected to have $89.7 million in available cap space in 2027, more than any other franchise. The injury landed Jackson on injured reserve. Head coach Jesse Minter has told reporters that it could "potentially" end the quarterback's season. Since Jackson's injury, his future beyond 2026 has become a major topic of discussion. He has just one year left on his current deal, a very tricky contract situation, and enough injury concerns that some have questioned whether Baltimore will consider going in a different direction in 2027. home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. My Bengals vs. Falcons prediction has Cincinnati packing extra luggage to carry its momentum to Madrid, where the Bengals look to extend their winning ways against Atlanta on Sunday morning. Cincinnati is laying just over a field goal inside Santiago Bernabéu Stadium and is riding a three-game streak into Week 9, though it built that run against some softer opposition. Read on for the edges in this international encounter and my best NFL picks to wake up to on Sunday, Nov. 8, starring Tee Higgins. Bengals vs Falcons prediction: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. Projections call for another big day, with most models north of 80 yards receiving from Higgins. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards TOP PICK Bengals vs Falcons player prop: Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards Bengals receiver Tee Higgins is coming off a monster day versus Tennessee, drawing 11 targets for 10 catches and 155 yards. Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league, with Ja'Marr Chase drawing the ire of the secondary and leaving the 6-foot-4 Higgins with softer matchups. He gets a perfect pairing against Atlanta in Madrid. The Falcons rank 24th in DVOA defending WR2s , allowing an average of 54.6 yards per game to the position. This secondary is also running a high rate of man coverage (10th most), and Higgins currently rates as the No. 1 WR versus man at PFF. Projections for Higgins range from 74 to 88 yards on Sunday morning, with most models north of 80 yards. My number comes out to 81.5 receiving yards in Madrid. Want more NFL player props? They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Though they did not look good against the Titans last week. Regardless, both teams are hungry for a win and have all the offensive weapons needed to get it done. Here are three bold predictions ahead of this huge international clash between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. Now sitting at 3-5—along with the rest of the division—Atlanta is in a difficult place. Games against some of the AFC and NFC's best await over the next month, sandwiched around the team's Week 11 bye. The first game in this sequence comes early Sunday morning in Madrid, as the Falcons take on the Bengals. Cincinnati is a bit volatile, but possesses one of the best offenses in the NFL led by quarterback Joe Burrow and the elite receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Right now, the Falcons are 3-point underdogs against the Bengals, per FanDuel. Atlanta needs a victory to stay afloat in the playoff hunt, but can it come against this Cincinnati team? Let's take a closer look. Falcons vs Bengals Week 9 predictions The Bengals hold the NFL's second-best scoring offense, best third-down offense, and are also top-10 in total yardage. This will be one of the biggest tests for Atlanta's defense all season. The good news for the Falcons is that Cincinnati's offense is very one-dimensional, with the vast majority of their production coming via the passing game. Over the past few weeks, Atlanta's biggest issue has been stopping the run. That shouldn't be a problem in Week 9, as the Bengals are 30th in rushing yardage and 28th in yards per carry. Atlanta has been outstanding generating interior pressure and pretty solid outside, but has lacked a true finisher to pile up sacks. Pearce brings that ability, and will hopefully bring a big boost to the defensive line on passing downs. On the other side of the ball, the message is simple: the Falcons offense must get back on track, and can't afford to start slow. This game has the potential to be a "Bijan takeover" performance, with Cincinnati 29th in yards per carry allowed on defense. Bijan got a bit stuck in the mud against Tampa Bay, and I think he'll have an explosive game in Madrid. All in all, it likely comes down to the Falcons ability to limit the Bengals offensive chances by holding the ball as much as possible, and capitalizing on their own scoring opportunities. away.headline: Bengals LB Demetrius Knight Jr injured vs Titans in NFL Week 8
away.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. was injured during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 8 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium. Knight was injured during a 41-yard touchdown run by Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. Knight remained down on the field at the end of the play. Knight jogged off the field under his own power, and went to the blue medical tent for evaluation. Knight returned to the game on the Titans' next drive. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Knight had a huge play during the third quarter when he tackled Pollard in the end zone for a safety to give Cincinnati a 23-21 lead. "What a big-time play by a big-time player in Demetrius Knight," CBS analyst Robert Turbin said during the broadcast. Knight, the Bengals' second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, is in his second season with the team. Knight was injured during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. Knight returned to the game early in the second quarter. Knight left the game during the fourth quarter in the team's NFL Week 1 win against Tampa Bay, with apparent cramping. Earlier in the game, Knight scored the Bengals' first touchdown of the season on a fumble recovery for a score. In 2025, Knight suffered muscle cramps and went to the locker room during the second half of the team's NFL Week 9 loss to Chicago at Paycor Stadium. One week earlier, during the team's NFL Week 8 loss to the New York Jets, Knight remained down on the field after a collision with Jets rookie tight end Mason Taylor, but walked off under his own power. Knight suffered a leg injury in September 2025 during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 4 loss to Denver. He walked off the field under his own power, returned to the game later in the second quarter, and had his first career interception in the end zone near the end of the first half. Knight wore a Joe Burrow jersey as he arrived at the stadium in Denver. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Bengals' Demetrius Knight Jr returns from injury for safety vs Titans

Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. away.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
away.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. Speaking of the secondary, safeties Caleb Downs and PJ Locke remain in the concussion protocol. Each was upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday. NFL players who enter the protocol often miss at least one week, but there's no set minimum number of days a player has to sit. At least Downs and Locke took a significant step forward by getting back to on-field activity as limited participants. away.headline: Jets announce concerning injury update on WR Garrett Wilson
away.blurb: The New York Jets could be without their No. 1 wide receiver weapon in Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. When speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced that Garrett Wilson is in the NFL ‘s concussion protocol and considered “day-to-day” moving forward. “Garrett, he’s in the concussion protocol. He’ll be day-to-day,” Glenn said. Wilson, who’s been openly frustrated about his role in the Jets’ offense so far this season, had six catches for 83 yards in this past Sunday’s 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson’s practice status later this week will be a good indication of his potential availability for Sunday’s road matchup against the Chiefs. Fortunately for the Jets, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is back from injury and performing at a high level. In Sunday’s loss to the Raiders, he paced New York with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. Rookie pass catcher Omar Cooper Jr. has also flashed brilliance on a few occasions in his debut campaign. Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs will kick off at 1 p.m. ET from Arrowhead Stadium. Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. Miami Dolphins Game Preview and Score Prediction (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen · Roundtable Sports Sat, November 7, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (5-2) are packing their bags for a sunny South Beach showdown this Sunday, November 8, as they take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) at Hard Rock Stadium. Scheduled for a 1:00 PM EST kickoff, this Week nine matchup presents a stark contrast in team trajectories, but a closer look at the statistical landscape reveals exactly where this game will be won and lost. A Clash of Statistical Extremes The statistical tale of the tape paints a picture of a dominant Detroit squad matching up against a struggling Miami franchise. The Lions boast one of the NFL's most explosive offenses, ranking third in the league by averaging 29.0 points per game and holding the crown as the #1 total offense with an incredible 412.0 total yards per contest. Detroit's balanced attack features the fourth-ranked passing game (280.6 yards per game) paired with a punishing seventh-ranked ground assault (131.4 yards per game). In stark contrast, Jeff Hafley's Dolphins have struggled to find a rhythm all year. Miami ranks near the bottom of the league in almost every major offensive category, sitting at 31st in points per game (16.7) and 28th in total yards per game (304.4). Their aerial attack has been particularly stagnant, ranking 31st while averaging a mere 181.1 passing yards per game. Exploiting the Matchups The primary catalyst for a Lions blowout lies in the mismatch between Detroit's high-powered passing attack and Miami's secondary. The Dolphins sit 17th in total defense (334.1 yards allowed per game) and 16th against the pass (221.0 yards allowed per game). However, they have struggled immensely to rush the passer, recording just nine sacks all season (30th in the NFL). With Jared Goff protected by an elite offensive line, he should have all day to pick apart a secondary that lacks a consistent pass rush up front. Furthermore, while Miami's offense has a respectable ground game averaging 123.3 yards per game (eleventh), they run right into the teeth of a fierce Detroit run defense. The Lions allow just 96.6 rushing yards per game, ranking ninth in the NFL. By neutralizing Miami's ground game, the Lions can force the Dolphins into obvious passing situations, where Detroit's defense, which has already racked up 24 sacks this year (third in the NFL), can relentlessly hunt the quarterback. Overcoming the Flaws If there is a vulnerability for Detroit to watch out for, it is their 32nd-ranked pass defense, which surrenders a massive 276.6 yards per game through the air. Additionally, Miami actually holds the statistical edge in third-down efficiency, converting at a 42.7% clip (9th) compared to Detroit's 39.0% (14th). However, Miami's inefficient passing game is uniquely poorly suited to exploit Detroit's secondary weakness. Without an explosive downfield element, the Dolphins will find it incredibly difficult to keep pace on the scoreboard, especially with Detroit controlling the clock via a dominant 30:59 to 28:47 time of possession advantage. Prediction: Lions Suffocate the Dolphins Expect the Lions to lean on Jahmyr Gibbs early to test Miami's 16th-ranked run defense, setting up devastating play-action shots downfield to Amon-Ra St. Brown . Defensively, Detroit's front four will collapse the pocket against a weak Miami offensive line, forcing turnovers and short drives. The Lions have too much firepower, too much balance, and a massive edge in the trenches. Detroit handles business cleanly, silencing the home crowd and easily covering the seven-point road spread. Final Score Prediction: Detroit Lions 34, Miami Dolphins 16

picks.headline: Lions vs. Dolphins 5 Qs preview: Is Miami mirroring Detroit’s 2021 culture rebuild?
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Dolphins 5 Qs preview: Is Miami mirroring Detroit’s 2021 culture rebuild? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Dan Campbell guides the Lions through workouts during a spring minicamp. 2022-06-10 Dan Campbell | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ryan Mathews · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions head to South Beach for a Week 9 interconference matchup against a young, rebuilding Miami Dolphins team. We had the pleasure of connecting with Kevin Nogle, the Managing Editor of Phinsider to give us some insight into this Miami team ahead of Sunday's kickoff. We learned about the local sentiment surrounding head coach Jeff Hafley's foundational reset, how offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik is tailoring the offense to quarterback Malik Willis, and how Ollie Gordon is handling the backfield workload in De'Von Achane's absence—plus what Miami needs to do to keep pace with Detroit's offense. 1. Miami arguably made more changes to their organization than any other team in the NFL this offseason. New head coach, new quarterback, the changing out of long-tenured skill position players—it was a massive overhaul in South Beach. Although the Dolphins are off to a 1-6 start, how much of that was expected from a team that underwent so many changes this offseason? It's early, but do you get the sense that new head coach Jeff Hafley is the right guy for this rebuild? This year is about setting up the franchise for the future, and while losses are never fun, the struggles were expected. This is the league's youngest team, and they are facing a steep learning curve. Miami has 14 rookies on the roster, plus another seven first-year players. This is clearly a reset of the team's foundation, and there will be growing pains. The Dolphins' schedule has also been brutal this year. They started the year against the Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, and Minnesota Vikings, not facing a team that had a loss until Week 5 against the Cincinnati Bengals, who were 2-2 coming into that game. Through Week 8, Miami has faced the league's toughest schedule, with a combined opponent winning percentage of .589. The schedule is not an excuse, but with such a young team, it is another variable to consider. Obviously, things can change, but Hafley has instilled confidence in the fanbase so far. The Mike McDaniel era had some fun moments, but it quickly fell apart and the team never adjusted (and McDaniel still does not seem to have made adjustments as the Los Angeles Chargers struggle this year). I think Hafley's focus on making the Dolphins physical, allowing the younger players to gain experience, and the team's ability to make adjustments, learn from mistakes, and continue to fight even in losing situations indicate he is the right guy for this role. Lions fans saw Dan Campbell build a culture out of tough losses back in 2021; that is exactly the phase Hafley and the Dolphins are in right now. 2. From the outside looking in, Malik Willis was dropped into a tough situation given the pieces around him in the offense—and it looks like, predictably, the passing game has struggled so far. The Dolphins rank 26th in passing DVOA and EPA/pass. How has Bobby Slowik tried to tailor this offense to Willis' strengths? What's working, what's not working, and how much of that is related to a new quarterback in a new system versus the lack of talent personnel-wise? I think we are starting to see Willis find some comfort in the offensive system, and he is starting to play better. Despite being a third-round pick in 2022, Willis has played in only 29 career games, starting just 13. He is a league veteran but really has the starting experience of a rookie. At times, he still seems bothered by the speed of the game, but the experience he is getting this year is already making a difference in his play. I think one of the biggest issues we have seen from Willis is a desire to be a pocket passer. He stays in the pocket longer than he should, trying to find the perfect pass rather than taking something shorter or throwing the ball away to avoid a sack. The offensive line is not doing him any favors, but he has taken multiple sacks by running out of bounds instead of throwing the ball away. He seemed to want to avoid using his legs, but has opened up that part of his game in the last couple of weeks. Slowik, like McDaniel before him, has an offensive system built on quarterback accuracy and timing. He uses bootlegs, run-pass options, and play-action passes to get Willis out of the pocket and seeing open receivers. They also seem to be using some half-field concepts, keeping Willis looking in one area and working from deep to shallow rather than having him search the entire field for receivers. The youth on the roster – especially with wide receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman Jr. – do not always create separation, and drops have also been an issue. When the primary target is not open on time, a young quarterback hesitates, and behind an evolving offensive line, hesitation leads to sacks. That all relates back to the discussion of Miami's reset this year. The potential for talent is on Miami's roster, but they still need to grow individually and together. The coaching staff is clearly working on the balance between youth and system – relying on a more basic system as the players learn. 3. Losing De'Von Achane in the first month of the season felt especially cruel for this offense that was already so limited on difference makers. The Dolphins rank 9th in EPA/rush (-0.03) but rank near the bottom of the league in rush success rate (26th) and rush DVOA (26th), suggesting that their run game is a boom-or-bust attack. Is that a fair assessment of Ollie Gordon's performance this year? The Dolphins also rank 26th in stuffed rate (22.8%) which is the percentage of runs that earn zero or negative yards. Are those stuffed runs more of an indictment of the offensive line or the coaching/play calling? That seems like a fair assessment. Gordon has been a lot of fun to watch as he breaks out this year, but he is a power-back who works extremely well as a change-of-pace option behind Achane. When he finds space, he is able to break it for a big gain, but it really is boom or bust on each run. Part of that is Gordon and his abilities. Part of that is the offensive line finding space to get him free. And part of that is opposing defenses planning to stop the run. Miami has had success this year, averaging 131 rushing yards per game, and they have topped 100 yards in five of seven games, including one game over 150 yards and another over 200 yards. They also have two games with 74 yards rushing each. Boom or bust. The offensive line—especially last week with Kadyn Proctor out with a concussion—still has work to do to come together as a unit. I think play calling is part of it, but not necessarily because the plays are wrong, but rather because the player is wrong. The rushing attack was built for Achane's skill set, complemented by Gordon. Now, it is a Gordon-led unit and some of the designs are clearly meant for Achane's speed over Gordon's power. We have seen that evolve as Slowik has adjusted to Gordon, but there is an obvious difference between the two players and there will likely be a boom or bust aspect to the Dolphins' ground game all season. The outside zone, stretch concepts were designed for Achane's elite sideline-to-sideline track speed. Gordon is a one-cut, downhill runner. The Dolphins have pivoted to more gap and inside-zone looks to match Gordon's style, but until defenses are forced to back out of the box, stops will linger. 4. Hafley brings his decades of experience coaching defense to Miami, and the numbers related to personnel deployment and coverage usage are pretty interesting through eight weeks. Miami lines up in base personnel 51.7% of snaps, second-most in the NFL, and they're utilizing zone coverage 78.8% of the time (10th in the NFL). How much of these numbers overlap with the talent available on the current roster? In other words, does it feel like Hafley's trying to put his players in the best spots to succeed? Numbers suggest the run defense is bordering on being a top-10 unit, but the pass defense might be the worst in the league. Do those numbers tell the whole story? Hafley definitely relies on base defense and he expects his front four to create pressure, rather than relying on the blitz—especially when compared to someone like Brian Flores, a former Dolphins head coach, and his blitz heavy defense. Hafley expects the pressure to come from the front four, allowing him to keep additional players back in coverage or focused on the run. It has been successful—at least as successful as can be expected with the younger players executing on the field. The run defense has been strong for much of the year. There have been mistakes, especially when an edge rusher bites on a play action, chasing the quarterback and failing to set the edge or runs right past the ball carrier, but overall, they are doing well against the run. Of course, I say all of that knowing full well Jahmyr Gibbs is second in the league in rushing and is averaging nearly five-yards-per-carry, so the pressure is on the defense to continue to find success this week. Does the contrast between the pass defense and the run defense tell the entire story? Not necessarily. The heavy zone scheme with the younger defensive backs is designed to prevent explosive, 60+ yard plays. That is allowing for short and intermediate routes to pick apart defenses (especially when Miami struggles to cover tight ends. Good thing the Lions are not bringing a top-tier tight end into this game, right?!?). Add in that Miami has been playing from behind for much of the year, and the short, possession passing game has been highly effective. I do think Hafley is keeping his defensive calls a little more basic than maybe we will see from him in the next few years, allowing the foundation to be set before he starts building off of it. The Dolphins have stressed that they expect to build for the future through the draft and grow the team from within. If they stick to that plan, I think you will see both the offense and defense evolve as the players grow and Miami moves from a roster dominated by rookies to one with veterans hitting their prime supported by key rookies each year. 5. The Dolphins opened as 7-point home underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook heading into this Week 9 matchup against the Lions. What's one thing you want to see, what's one thing you need to see, and one thing you're sure you'll see happen in this matchup between the Lions and Dolphins on Sunday afternoon? I want to see the offense be aggressive and take shots downfield. The Lions are allowing 276 yards per game through the air, and they are banged up. Let Willis test them early, get Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell into the game, and use the play-action to create opportunities. The Dolphins need to come into this game feeling like they have to win in a shoot-out. If they are aggressive on offense, maybe they can catch the Lions a little flat-footed at the start. I need to see the Dolphins continue to make adjustments week-to-week, correct mistakes from the last game, and grow as a unit. That will be true throughout this season. away.headline: NFL-Lions report positive progress for linebacker Campbell after injury
away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

away.blurb: Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week. Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement: Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified. Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return. Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday’s practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend’s game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability. Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back. Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth. The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell’s comments throughout the week. home.headline: Lions, Dolphins week 9 injury designations: Lions rule out 5 starters
home.blurb: Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week. Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement: Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified. Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return. Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday’s practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend’s game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability. Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back. Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth. The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell’s comments throughout the week. Let’s look at Friday’s practice report and get you up to date on what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . home.headline: Lions vs. Dolphins injury report: Jaylen Wright does not practice; Jack Campbell update
home.blurb: If Wright is unable to play this weekend, rookie running back Kaytron Allen, the Washington Commanders' sixth-round pick who Miami claimed off waivers last month, could be in line to backup Ollie Gordon II. Allen, however, was limited in practice with a quadriceps injury of his own.
