(Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Nogle · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins' second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright's contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday's practice but remains in the league's concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. "He is progressing in the protocol," Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor's place last week. Good news from Detroit's Jack Campbell The Lions' All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger

(Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the New Orleans Saints this Sunday. The Browns are coming off of a bad loss to the Steelers, but it looks like they'll have a change at quarterback this week (forced by injury) with Shedeur Sanders being under center. The Saints are well-rested, coming off of a bye. Note that some of the picks below were written up before the Browns' quarterback news. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson's 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken's offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints' defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson's release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Saints 17, Browns 14 The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Browns 20, Saints 17 Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Saints 23, Browns 20 The Browns are quickly regressing to the mean and going into a hostile environment to face a hungry, young team after a bye doesn't bode well. New Orleans will have emphasized the need to execute better at home for both Kellen Moore and Brandon Staley. Tyler Shough gets it done, having more reliable weapons than Deshaun Watson. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Saints 20, Browns 17 Both offenses are struggling. Deshaun Watson has taken a league-high 33 sacks, and the Browns average 97.6 rushing yards per game. New Orleans has been worse on the ground, but a bye week comes at the right time. The Saints are 0-4 S/U this season – and this game is a candidate for a walk-off field goal either way. Tyler Shough needs to avoid the interceptions, but New Orleans wins a coin-flip game. Below are our Week 9 NFL staff picks:

picks.headline: Staff picks: Final score, bold predictions for Saints vs. Browns
picks.blurb: Staff picks: Final score, bold predictions for Saints vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Staff picks: Final score, bold predictions for Saints vs. Browns John Sigler, Arye Pulli, Bob Rose , Jeremy Trottier and Luke Loffredo, Saints Wire · Saints Wire Sat, November 7, 2026 at 10:55 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads How do you see this one playing out? The New Orleans Saints (2-5) are coming out of their bye week for a home game with the Cleveland Browns (5-3) at the Caesars Superdome, and they could be getting a break. Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is replacing the starter, Deshaun Watson, who missed practice this week with concussion symptoms. But the Saints can't take anything for granted. They haven't earned that yet. Here are our staff picks with final scores and bold predictions for Week 9's game. Saints 23, Browns 20 Every game should be a must-win for Kellen Moore's team after they lost five of their first seven matchups. The Saints at least need to show visible growth week over week after falling into a monthslong slump. We don't know yet if Jordyn Tyson or Kelvin Banks Jr. will be back on the field, but getting either of the team's last two first-round picks would give the offense a big boost. Either way, Cleveland doesn't do anything exceptionally well despite their 5-3 record (to that point: they haven't won a single game by more than four points). They're league-average in rates of allowing touchdown passes and intercepting them, with a comparable sacks rate to New Orleans. Their run defense is almost as porous as the New York Giants unit we watched the Saints bulldoze a few weeks ago. This is a winnable game for the Saints, especially with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback. But they aren't a good enough team to feel too great about themselves no matter who the opponent is. Bold prediction: Charlie Smyth kicks a game-winning field goal as time expires. -- John Sigler Saints 27, Browns 16 The Saints have now had two weeks to reset after their trip to Paris and they draw a favorable matchup with Shedeur Sanders getting the start. Shough finds his rhythm despite Cleveland's secondary, while New Orleans takes advantage of a Browns offensive line that has allowed an NFL-high 4.1 sacks per game. The Saints earn their first home win of the season and remain alive in the NFC South race. Bold prediction: Tyler Shough throws three touchdowns against Cleveland's sixth-ranked passing defense. -- Arye Pulli Saints 24, Browns 13 You can't call this a 'get right' game for a Saints team that's done very little right this season. However, this should be a good matchup for New Orleans against a Cleveland team that's struggled offensively and will likely be without quarterback Deshaun Watson and Maliek Collins on defense. In this one, the Saints run the ball just well enough to establish balance and set up some big plays with Tyler Shough and the passing game. Defensively, New Orleans pummels Shadeur Sanders into several sacks and a few costly turnovers to finally get their first win of the year in the Superdome. Bold prediction: New Orleans holds Cleveland to under 300 total yards, the first time the Saints have done that to an opponent this season. -- Bob Rose Browns 24, Saints 17 The New Orleans Saints had their chance to rest and recuperate during the bye week, and are immediately faced with an extremely interesting test with the Cleveland Browns on deck. With Shedeur Sanders expected to start in place of Deshaun Watson, it should be interesting to see what he can do with a half-season of preparation since his last start. The Saints have been unstable both on defense and in the run game, and are facing a team allowing only 196.6 pass yards per game, No. 6 in the NFL. This will be an enormous test of if New Orleans can either run or beat out an exceptionally strong secondary, and in all reality, they've shown little to be confident in for either category. Bold prediction: The Saints are held under 250 total scrimmage yards on the day. -- Jeremy Trottier Saints 23, Browns 10 With Deshaun Watson's status in doubt for this matchup, the New Orleans Saints have a much better chance of taking down a stingy Cleveland Browns team. If Watson is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders is prepared to step in under center, which could create opportunities for the Saints' pass rush to get home against a less mobile quarterback. If New Orleans can take care of business defensively and find ways to put points on the board against an aggressive Browns defense, the Saints should be in a good position to come away with a victory at home. Bold prediction: Saints defense records 5 sacks. -- Luke Loffredo This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Staff picks: Final score, bold predictions for Saints vs. Browns

picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints Jeffrey Olson, Browns Wire · Browns Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:55 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are looking to keep pace in the playoff race this weekend. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. However, I don't think this game will be way off from that in terms of production. As stated before, the Saints have a bad run defense. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. This pairs with the Browns' advantage, as the Saints are 6th in the NFL in most giveaways. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game. picks.headline: Experts Aren't Sold on Browns to Defeat Saints in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Aren't Sold on Browns to Defeat Saints in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Experts Aren't Sold on Browns to Defeat Saints in Week 9 (Steve Roberts-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:52 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns will be entering Week 9 of the season looking to grab a bounce-back win over the New Orleans Saints Cleveland dropped its game last week to the Pittsburgh Steelers, seeing their record fall to 5-3 on the season. The Browns are currently in third place within the AFC North division, with the team still thinking about a possible playoff run. While the loss to the Steelers was very disappointing for the Browns, the team still has the utmost confidence as it enters the game this week. However, the Browns will likely be playing the game with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, with starter Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. It remains to be seen if Sanders will be starting the game, but at this point, it's trending toward happening . Sanders did play last season for the Browns, going 3-4 as a starter at the end of the year. As for New Orleans, they will be coming into the game with a record of 2-5 on the season, but the team did have a bye this past week. New Orleans has gone 0-4 at home this year, giving the Browns some extra ammo going into the week. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report predicted how the contest would go this week. Among these picks, only two of the seven chose Cleveland to go on the road to win this week. O'Donnell and Sobleski were the two to choose the Browns to grab the win this week over the Saints. Cleveland's defense has the talent to keep them in this game, but the offense is likely going to have to win it. For the Browns, whoever is under center will be tasked with getting this team back on track. The offense has sputtered over the last few weeks, and this is an area that Cleveland wants to get back going strong. New Orleans can be a sneaky team, even with their lackluster record on the season, with them having beaten the Baltimore Ravens, with a healthy Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and New York Giants this year. The Saints were expected to be better than where they currently are, so the Browns will need to be careful. Kickoff for this game will take place at 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans.

away.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Patrick Gorski/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are heading into their Week 9 matchup with a 5-3 record, looking to keep pace with the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC North. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. MORE : Joe Burrow joins rare NFL history with six touchdowns despite three interceptions With Harold Fannin Jr., Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Denzel Boston, and KC Concepcion, Sanders has a much better supporting cast this season than he did for much of last year. Sanders is the Browns' Week 9 starter against the Saints, which will be his first real chance to play in his second NFL season after a Pro Bowl rookie year. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. picks.blurb: Eagles vs. Giants predictions for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Eagles vs. Giants predictions for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season NBC Sports Philadelphia Staff · NBC Sports Philadelphia Sat, November 7, 2026 at 7:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Eagles vs. Giants predictions for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Eagles (2-6) host the first-place New York Giants (4-2-1) in an NFC battle at the Linc on Sunday afternoon. Let's get to our predictions: Reuben Frank (6-2) I'm not sure how good the Giants are, but I do know how bad the Eagles are. Really bad. Seems like John Harbaugh has done a nice job transforming the Giants' culture from losing to winning almost overnight. The Giants are 4-2-1, just the second time in the last decade they've had a winning record eight games into a season. This is the first time the Eagles and Giants will meet with the Giants at least two games over .500 and the Eagles at least two games under .500 since 2016, when the Giants were 10-4 going into a late-season game against the Eagles at the Linc and the Eagles were 5-9. The Eagles won that one 24-19 behind Carson Wentz, who was teammates with current Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy in Minnesota earlier this year. Anyway, hopefully Joe Milton injects some life into the offense, but I just don't think the Eagles are good enough to beat anybody right now. Seven in a row? Really? Really. Giants 27, Eagles 21 Dave Zangaro (7-1) Have I lost my mind? Maybe. But I have a gut feeling about this game that the Eagles are going to snap their losing streak. This is not a prediction that they're about to turn around their season or that Joe Milton is some sort of great answer. Just that inserting Milton into the offense will provide a bit of a spark and the Eagles will finally be able to scrape out a low-scoring game against another QB who wasn't with his team when the year began. The Giants have been playing tough, but I'm not a real believer. We know the Giants are going to blitz the heck out of the Eagles, but at least Milton will be able to get away from some of that pressure and give the Eagles a chance to create. The Giants might not have Cam Skattebo, which would really hurt their offense and make them more one-dimensional. If that's the case, then the Eagles might actually be able to finally get some pressure on the QB. If the Eagles win this game, the defense will probably have to force a couple turnovers and I think they can finally do that. Is this the wisest prediction of the year? No way. I don't really want to pick the Eagles but I'm going with my gut. A win before the bye week — a win that should not change any decisions ahead of the trade deadline. Eagles 21, Giants 17 Mike Mulhern (5-3) Considering what we've seen from the Eagles over the last six weeks, it's shocking to see they're only 3.5 point underdogs at home to the first-place Giants. The switch from Tanner McKee to Joe Milton didn't have much impact on the betting line, but it should at least increase the watchability factor of Sunday's game. Milton has the physical tools to be an NFL starter but has yet to show he can put it all together. It was surprising to see him cut by the Cowboys after an impressive preseason. He even went unclaimed on waivers, letting you know the entire league didn't even see him as a backup. After settling in on the practice squad in Dallas, he's now starting for the Eagles less than a month after being signed to the 53-man roster by Howie Roseman. The timing of the switch – with the bye week looming – is quite curious. They could have waited and a game and given Milton a two-week runway into his first NFL start. Perhaps this Tuesday's trade deadline has something to do with it. Either way, the Eagles should get a spark but it won't be enough to beat John Harbaugh's bunch. The Giants play tough and have stars in the trenches. JJ McCarthy has a new lease on his NFL life and is making the most of it. He sends the Eagles into their week off on a seven-game skid. Giants 24, Eagles 20 Ashlyn Sullivan (5-3) Joe Milton takes over as the Eagles' starting quarterback, and I think the element of the unknown could actually work in Philadelphia's favor. There is very little film on Milton, and even the Eagles themselves may not know exactly what to expect from a quarterback making his first career start. Sometimes, that's a good thing. Don't overthink it — just go out and play. Saquon Barkley should also be a little healthier after getting another week of rest for his hamstring and back, which could allow Milton to lean heavily on the Eagles' running game. That's why I expect this game to be close. However, it's difficult to make a strong case for the Eagles winning another game until they show they can consistently move the football and generate some offense through the air. On the other side, I've been impressed with what New York has been able to accomplish despite having a relatively average roster. Credit the Giants' coaching staff for getting the most out of this group. Matt Nagy has been a strong offensive addition, and quarterback JJ McCarthy appears to be giving the Giants a spark as they look to make some noise in the NFC East. Giants 24, Eagles 17 Ryan Fowler (7-1) As much uncertainty that there is surrounding Joe Milton's first career start, expect some fireworks on Sunday against the Giants. Milton is as talented a thrower of the football as I've seen up close, as the ball just pops out his hand with a type of velocity matched by few on Earth. That's the honest truth. However, there is much more to succeeding at the NFL level than just having a howitzer for an arm, and that's where it starts this week for Milton and the Eagles' offensive coaching staff. Minimizing the playbook and focusing on what he does best (RPOs, bootleg, designed QB runs) will remain paramount if the Eagles want to leave Week 9 with a win. The offense as a whole hasn't looked good at all whoever has been under center, which leaves me with little confidence that the metaphorical lightbulb will click on this week, but you should be very excited about the skillset that Milton possesses. There will be plays that make a highlight reel, and plays that make you scratch your head, but why not let him go rip it this week. Let's just hope the offensive line gives him a few seconds to go through his progressions, as Giants DC Dennard Wilson won't be shy in heating him up. Defensively, muddy up looks as much as you can against JJ McCarthy. He thrives in rhythm and in the intermediate areas. Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, the focus is on the guys off the edge to create some push this week. The Giants leave their tackles on an island a bunch, and if you can create some push 1-on-1 there should be opportunities to force a few turnovers. Overall, I just don't trust this team right now to play complementary football for a full 60 minutes. They have failed to show any type of adjustments in any of the three phases of the game week after week, and their opponent in the Giants have a true identity as a football team who are playing some good ball right now. Giants 26, Eagles 17

Skattebo sustained a hamstring injury at the end of a big run in overtime of Week 7’s win over the Houston Texans. Despite having a full week to recover over the Giants’ bye, it appears he won’t be ready to go for Sunday’s Week 9 clash against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles. With Tyrone Tracy Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury of his own, the Giants are thin at the running back position. Devin Singletary will serve as the Giants’ lead back in Week 9, likely backed up by Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah. After not recording a single touch or carry in Week 6, Skattebo bounced back with a big performance in Week 7 — taking 17 carries for 124 yards and a touchdown. The Giants are 4-2-1 to begin the 2026 NFL season, leading the NFC East. They can extend their lead in the division with a win over the injury-ridden Eagles on Sunday. However, Stafford had a rather relaxed response when reporters asked about his condition on Wednesday, November 4. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. In fact, he joked that reporters had only recently started noticing something he had been doing throughout the season. "You guys have been blind. away.headline: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week. Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career. However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up. Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far. Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today. Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week. The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

home.blurb: Garrett has been working his way back from knee surgery that forced him onto IR after the season opener. After missing the Rams’ last several games, the defensive standout has returned to practice this week, and all indications point toward him being available against Washington. Getting Garrett back would provide a significant lift for a Los Angeles defense preparing for an important road matchup. Myles Garrett trending toward return against Commanders Garrett’s return to the field has been one of the biggest injury developments for the Rams heading into Week 9. The pass rusher underwent knee surgery in September after experiencing issues with the knee, and the procedure ultimately forced him to miss an extended stretch of the season. Los Angeles opened Garrett’s 21-day practice window this week, allowing him to return to the field while the organization evaluates his readiness to come off Injured Reserve. Head coach Sean McVay initially emphasized that the team would take the process day by day rather than establish a firm timetable for his return. Garrett has made progress throughout the week, and the latest report indicates that the Rams are preparing to activate him ahead of Sunday’s game. He was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice, an encouraging development considering he had not practiced since the season opener. The final step is getting him officially activated and ready to return to game action. The Rams made a substantial investment to acquire Garrett, and getting him back on the field is an important development for an organization with significant expectations. While his return does not automatically guarantee an immediate return to his usual level of production, having him available would give the defense another difference-maker. There is also a big difference between having Garrett available in practice and having him ready to contribute during a regular-season game. After knee surgery and an extended absence, the Rams will want to make sure he is physically prepared before putting him back into the lineup. After spending weeks waiting for their star pass rusher to return, Los Angeles could finally have him back on the field this weekend. That would be a significant development for the Rams as they look to strengthen their defense for the second half of the NFL season. picks.headline: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos?
picks.blurb: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Christopher Mason · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers are coming off a mini-bye week following their Thursday night football loss to the Green Bay Packers . Now, they prepare to welcome one of the AFC's top teams, the Denver Broncos . Denver travels to Charlotte following a close win against its division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. This will be the ninth meeting between the two teams, with the Broncos holding a 7-2 advantage over Carolina, including their victory in Super Bowl 50. The Panthers enter this matchup barely holding on to their first-place lead in the NFC South and riding a two-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Broncos sit comfortably atop the AFC West and look to extend their lead against a struggling Carolina team. Both teams have their own issues. Carolina's defense has looked like a shell of itself while dealing with injuries and coaching changes. Denver's offense, meanwhile, has struggled to find consistency in the early stages of games, often waiting until the second half to hit its stride. Although the teams' records suggest a mismatch, this game presents an interesting study in how teams start versus how they finish. Green Bay Packers linebacker Ty'ron Hopper (59) is stiff-armed by Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 27-19. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Denver's Offense vs. Carolina's Defense The Denver Broncos are very much a second-half team, with their offense becoming more productive as games progress. Denver has generated 1,066 yards of total offense in the first half compared with 1,110 in the second half. The difference becomes more pronounced in the passing game, where the Broncos have recorded seven second-half passing touchdowns compared with just two in the first half. Bo Nix's yards per attempt also increased to 6.6 after halftime. The Panthers cannot afford to let Denver find its rhythm through the air. One way to prevent that is by generating consistent pressure on Nix, who has struggled against opposing blitzes. Carolina has had difficulty getting after the quarterback this season, with injuries taking a toll on its edge-rushing group. If the Panthers can disrupt Nix in the pocket, they could interrupt the rhythm that has allowed Denver to become more productive in the second half. Carolina must also find a way to stop the run. It is a message Coach Dave Canales has emphasized to new defensive coordinator Todd Wash . The Panthers have struggled against opposing rushing attacks, allowing approximately 140 yards per game on the ground. Denver uses its rushing attack to create favorable passing opportunities for Nix by forcing opposing safeties closer to the line of scrimmage. Running back Jonah Coleman also brings the speed to create problems for Carolina's defense at the second level. The Panthers showed some improvement against Green Bay, holding the Packers to fewer than 100 rushing yards while generating penetration from defensive tackles Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown. If Carolina can force Denver's running backs to deal with linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke, the Broncos could have a more difficult time creating the deep passing opportunities Nix prefers. Establishing control of the line of scrimmage will be critical to keeping Denver's offense in check. Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Lee Hunter (92) and linebacker Bobby Okereke (58) during warmups against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Can Carolina's Secondary Stop Bo Nix? The Carolina Panthers' secondary faces a productive touchdown scorer in Bo Nix. However, the Denver quarterback enters this matchup with some concerning passing efficiency numbers. Nix is averaging 6 yards per attempt while completing approximately 60% of his passes. He has also thrown nine touchdowns against three interceptions. His 83.6 passer rating further highlights some of the inconsistencies in Denver's passing attack. Those numbers present an opportunity for Carolina's secondary to disrupt the Broncos' aerial game. The Panthers will need to force Nix into difficult throws and make him take risks when attempting to push the ball downfield. However, Nix is particularly effective at extending plays and creating open passing lanes with his mobility in the pocket. Carolina's inability to generate a consistent pass rush could work in Denver's favor. If the Panthers cannot pressure Nix, he will have additional time to find receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle downfield. However, if Carolina's secondary can stay with Denver's receivers, Nix may be forced to extend plays and search for alternative passing windows. The Panthers must force Nix into difficult throwing angles and prevent him from creating open passing lanes over the middle of the field. Doing so could limit Denver's explosive plays while disrupting the timing of its offense. The longer Nix has to hold the football while searching for an open receiver, the more opportunities Carolina's defense will have to make a play. Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Bryce Young vs. the Broncos' Defense The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against Denver's defense. The Broncos enter this matchup tied for fourth in the NFL with 23 sacks. Bryce Young was sacked six times last week and has taken 11 sacks over the past two games. Young struggled to recognize pressure against Green Bay, while Carolina's offensive line consistently had difficulty giving him enough time to operate. This week, the Panthers' offensive line will have to contend with Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, and Zach Allen. All three have been among Denver's leading sack producers this season and have established themselves as key disruptors along the defensive front. Carolina will need to find ways to work around Denver's pass rush. That means incorporating quick passes, getting the football into the hands of its playmakers, and establishing a more consistent rushing attack. The Panthers do not have an elite running game, but Chuba Hubbard has shown the ability to break off explosive runs when given the opportunity. If Carolina can get Hubbard going early, it could open up the passing game, particularly through play-action. Carolina will also need to get creative with its receiver alignments. Tetairoa McMillan will likely see plenty of Denver's premier cornerback, Pat Surtain II. The Panthers should move McMillan around the formation to create more favorable matchups and prevent Denver from consistently deploying Surtain against Carolina's leading receiver. Similarly, if Jalen Coker is healthy enough to play at full strength, Carolina's receiving duo could give Denver some problems. Having multiple receiving threats available would make it more difficult for the Broncos to focus their coverage on McMillan. Ultimately, Young needs to get the football out quickly, avoid unnecessary sacks, and take advantage of the opportunities Denver's defense gives him. Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The Last Word The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against a tough opponent this week. While Carolina is struggling to keep its head above water, last week's game showed glimpses of the team fans had seen earlier in the season. The Panthers made a late push against Green Bay, fighting until the final seconds despite being outplayed for much of the night. If Carolina can keep Nix in check by forcing him to extend plays, disrupting his passing rhythm, and containing Denver's rushing attack, the defense could give the offense more opportunities to compete. On the offensive side of the ball, offensive coordinator Brad Idzik needs to return to some of the principles that made Carolina's offense successful earlier in the season. Establishing the run will go a long way toward opening up opportunities for the receivers while giving Young more time to make the throws he needs. If Carolina can execute complementary football and Todd Wash's defense shows signs of improvement under its new leadership, the Panthers could make this a competitive matchup. However, beating Denver will require four quarters of consistent football. Carolina cannot afford another slow start or a second-half collapse. Against a team that has made a habit of getting better as games progress, the Panthers will need to put together their most complete performance in weeks. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. Getty Tony Adame · HEAVY Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:06 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Denver Broncos need everyone on the field to beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday in Week 8 — especially after the shellacking the Chiefs handed the Broncos in the season opener, and because a Chiefs win would raise their odds of winning the AFC West Division to 83 percent. The Broncos got some good news in terms of help winning the game with an injury update for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on Sunday morning. "Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, who has been dealing with a chest injury that he aggravated last week, is trending in the right direction to play, source says," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on Sunday morning. Waddle was hurt late in a Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Chiefs Demolished Broncos, Waddle in Week 1 The Chiefs opened the season with a 31-10 blowout win over the Broncos in Week 1 — a game in which Waddle had 1 reception for 2 yards on 3 targets. Not really what you want for a player the Broncos gave up a 1st-round pick for in a March trade with the Miami Dolphins . Waddle has grossly underperformed so far this year. Even though the Broncos are 5-2, Waddle has just 26 receptions for 276 yards and 1 touchdown — he's also struggled with drops to this point. picks.headline: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference?
picks.blurb: Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers tight end David Njoku (83) limps off the field during the NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Michael Peterson · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:35 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. It's been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it's been just as rough when they've played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they'll add to that total this weekend given how things have gone for two months of the season now. Can they FINALLY shock the fan base and dig out their first win? Will the woes continue against Houston? I guess we have to tune in to find out. Here are the three things I'll be watching the closest when these two teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) How will the Chargers offense look with reinforcements en route? The Chargers offense will hopefully look a bit different this week with a pair starters returning to the fold. Tight end David Njoku had his activation window opened this week and has logged a pair of limited practices this week. He was one of Justin Herbert's top targets through the team's first two games and I'll be interested to see if that continues once he's back. Kayode Awosika, the team's starting left guard to begin the season, also looks to be making his way back to the field after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Awosika was one of the offensive line's best performance before going down with a fibula injury and I wouldn't be shocked if his presence next to Joe Alt on the left side moves the needle — in some way at least — on offense this week. Njoky being a pass-catching tight end first and forement could help the passing game while Awosika's return could potentially open up things on the ground. Now of course one player in each facet likely isn't enough to be a true fix, but that unit needs anything at all and two former starters returning to the field is a good start. 2.)Will the nightmare continue for Justin Herbert against the Texans? The last two times Justin Herbert and the Chargers have faced the Texans have been a nightmare. In last year's matchup on December 25th, the Chargers lost 20-16 in a game Herbert threw one touchdown to one interception. The prior game against Houston was the wild card matchup in January of '25 where Herbert threw four interceptions in one of his worst outings as a pro. As much as I wish I could say this is a real opportunity to exorcise the demons from those two games, I simply cannot. Herbert and the Chargers have never looked like a worse, less-cohesive unit and even with the Houston defense not its usual elite self, they still have numerous players who can make a splash play at a moment's notice. Even the return of a healthy Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Tre' Harris did next to nothing for the offense's production in Week Eight. Coming out of the bye, the Chargers scored just nine points, all of which came in the first half. They were then completely blanked in the second as Herbert threw his second interception on top of nearly losing a fumble that was luckily knocked out of bounds. At this rate, nothing is going to come to save the Chargers from themselves. If they want the nightmare to end, they've gotta wake up and do it themselves. 3.) Chargers pass defense will have another tough task vs. WR Nico Collins and a rejuvenated C.J. Stroud Stroud did not have to play at an All-Pro or Pro Bowl level the past two seasons while the Texans defense was arguably the best in the league from 2024-2025. This year, with the defense taking some steps back, he's had to carry the load a bit more and that's somewhat worked out after a rough start. The Texans are the NFL's 7th-ranked passing offense and that is mainly due to an abysmal run game averaging only 84.7 yards per game (29th). After throwing for at least 260 yards in Weeks Four through Six (including two games of over 300), Stroud only threw for 153 in their loss to the Giants just before their bye. With two weeks of preparation, you have to think they'll be ready to roll. On the flip side, the Chargers pass defense currently ranks 7th in the league, as well (198.4). That rank has mostly been maintained without All-Pro safety Derwin James or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson in the lineup. If that's not the far-and-away strength of the Bolts defense, then I don't know what is. Just a bunch of names putting together a top-10 unit under a first-year defensive coordinator. Will that be enough this week?

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Two of the league’s bigger disappointments meet Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium when the Chargers (0-7) host the Texans (2-5). Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. Houston then went back to SoFi Stadium in Week 17 last season and beat the Chargers 20-16, giving the Texans consecutive victories in the series for the first time. Things aren’t getting any better soon on that front, as the Chargers may put Derwin James on the IR with a hamstring injury. Outside of Biadasz, only seven players could return for the season. Rashawn Slater's absence is the most detrimental. The Chargers' offensive line entered the season with some major question marks, and that unit remains among the most worrisome. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 9 Upset Pick Minnesota Vikings (+150) vs. Buffalo Bills Josh Allen has a history of struggling against defenses as aggressive as the one Brian Flores operates. Allen did finally get by the Texans in Week 1, but that defense has drastically regressed this season. The Vikings’ defense has formed into what many expected to see out of the Texans in 2026. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). Yes, I do worry about Minnesota’s poor offense, but maybe Kyler Murray turns it around against the Bills’ poor defense, which is allowing 25.9 points per game. This will come down to Allen against the Vikings’ vaunted defense. Peter Dewey Week 9 Upset Pick Green Bay Packers (+140) vs. New England Patriots The Green Bay Packers can’t run the ball this season, averaging just 2.9 yards per carry, but that may not matter on the road against the New England Patriots in Week 9. New England is 20th in the league in EPA/Pass and eighth in EPA/Rush on defense, so the Packers and Jordan Love are likely going to lean on their elite passing game on Sunday. The Pack are coming off a mini-bye after playing on Thursday against Carolina, and they’ve won four of their last five games after a 1-2 start. Meanwhile, New England is extremely banged up at receiver and was in a dogfight against the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 8 before pulling away in the second half. The Pats have struggled a bit against elite competition this season, losing to Seattle, Jacksonville, and Chicago. Will we see a similar result against Green Bay? The Packers are quietly fifth in the NFL in EPA/Play on defense, and Love has been playing at a high level all season long. There aren’t a ton of great upset spots this week, but Green Bay’s recent form is intriguing against a banged-up New England squad. Iain MacMillan Week 9 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+240) vs. Chicago Bears You can win a lot of games in the National Football League if you can run the ball effectively and play elite defense, and that's exactly what the Buccaneers have been doing. In fact, they shut the Falcons out last week without completing a single pass. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team.
