picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. picks.headline: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

away.headline: Patriots get bad AJ Brown injury news ahead of Packers game
away.blurb: Now, it looks like Drake Maye will be without his No. 1 receiver once again, with head coach Mike Vrabel officially ruling Brown out for Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers. The fact that he’s been ruled out Sunday against the Packers isn’t entirely surprising given that he missed every practice this week. But it adds to Brown’s frustrating first season with the Patriots, and now there are even growing concerns about the condition of his knee, with some questioning how much longer he can truly keep playing at an elite level. As for Brown’s return, there’s no set timeline. He could be back next week against the Detroit Lions, which will be played in Munich, Germany, but with a Week 11 bye, the Patriots might also choose to play it safe and hold him out for that game as well. A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury in the New England Patriots ‘ season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks nearly two months ago. An MRI later confirmed it was a high ankle sprain, and the team placed him on Injured Reserve soon after, costing him the next four games. His Patriots debut ended with just three catches on four targets for 26 yards. Brown returned against the New York Jets in Week 6, but finished that game with three catches on 10 targets for a mere 27 yards, and then hauled in three catches for 48 yards the following week against the Chicago Bears. But he missed last week’s win over the Miami Dolphins with a knee issue and didn’t participate in practice all week. More news : Rams Get Major Myles Garrett Injury News Ahead of Commanders Game The latest report means Brown will now have missed six of nine games in his first season in New England. That’s not what Patriots fans were expecting when the team traded a first-round pick (and a fifth-rounder) to get him, or for a player making $32 million per year. Even in the three games he’s appeared in this year, Brown has been outplayed by the likes of Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, and Hunter Henry. More news : Patriots Get Concerning News as TreVeyon Henderson Reveals Health Scare More news : Jaguars’ Liam Coen Moves Ahead of 2 NFL Legends on All-Time Coaching List Without Brown, Maye will need to keep spreading the ball around. Douglas is New England’s leading receiver on the year with 26 catches for 332 yards and four touchdowns, followed by Henry with 29 catches for 326 yards and two touchdowns. Efton Chism III has also stepped up recently, hauling in a team-high five catches for 37 yards in last week’s win over the Dolphins. Those receivers should all have important roles against Green Bay. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. It was a different story against the Rams. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each ran for over 90 yards. Let's just say the 49ers aren't going up against the 2000 Ravens. picks.headline: Seahawks vs. Cardinals Week 9 game preview: Can Drew Lock repeat his Week 2 success?
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Cardinals Week 9 game preview: Can Drew Lock repeat his Week 2 success? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Alexandre Castro · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:14 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFC West matchup always carries extra weight, and Sunday's meeting between the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals is no exception. Seattle enters Week 9 with a 4-4 record after a disappointing 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears, while Arizona arrives at 3-5 following an impressive 33-30 overtime victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The two teams already met in Week 2, when Seattle dominated Arizona 31-7 on the road. Drew Lock started that game in place of an injured Sam Darnold, completing 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. Now, with Darnold sidelined once again, Lock is expected to get another opportunity against the Cardinals. There is, however, a different challenge awaiting Seattle this time around. Arizona has made a quarterback change of its own, turning to Gardner Minshew after Jacoby Brissett struggled to close out the game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Cardinals are coming off their best offensive performance of the season Arizona's comeback against Dallas was largely powered by two players: Gardner Minshew and Tyler Allgeier. After Jacoby Brissett struggled throughout the first half, completing just 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards and throwing an interception, head coach Mike LaFleur made the decision to turn to Minshew. The veteran quarterback immediately changed the complexion of the game. Minshew completed 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns, leading four consecutive touchdown drives to bring Arizona back from a 17-3 deficit. His connection with Michael Wilson was particularly important, with the receiver finishing the afternoon with eight catches for 111 yards and a touchdown, including the game-tying score with six seconds remaining. However, the biggest surprise was the Cardinals' running game. Tyler Allgeier (who would've been an amazing addition for the Seahawks in the last offseason…) exploded for 147 yards and a touchdown on just 11 carries, adding 44 receiving yards and another score. His performance was instrumental in Arizona's 33-30 overtime victory. That is an important development for Seattle. The Seahawks have had their own difficulties defending the run in the edge, and allowing Allgeier to find the same kind of space he enjoyed against Dallas could make this a much more difficult afternoon for Mike Macdonald's defense. There are still questions surrounding Arizona's backfield. Jeremiyah Love suffered another ankle injury against Dallas, while Bam Knight entered concussion protocol. Their availability will be worth monitoring throughout the week. Trey McBride remains Arizona's biggest receiving threat Even with the emergence of Michael Wilson, Trey McBride remains the centerpiece of Arizona's passing game. The tight end has recorded 66 receptions for 544 yards and five touchdowns this season, making him one of the most productive players at his position. Seattle has historically had difficulties containing McBride. His ability to find space between linebackers and safeties, particularly in the middle of the field, presents a challenging matchup for the Seahawks' defense. This becomes even more important considering some of Seattle's recent defensive struggles. The linebackers have had difficulties consistently covering the space behind them, and McBride is exactly the kind of player who can exploit those situations. If Arizona can establish a rhythm with Minshew, expect the Cardinals to look for their tight end frequently. Michael Wilson also deserves attention. Despite playing through fractured ribs, he managed to produce a big performance against Dallas. His availability and effectiveness will be important, particularly with Arizona looking to build on the chemistry developed with Minshew. Can Seattle's defensive line control the game again? The first meeting between these teams provided a pretty clear blueprint for Seattle. The Seahawks dominated the line of scrimmage, generated 18 quarterback pressures and limited Arizona to just 151 total yards. Jacoby Brissett struggled under pressure, completing only 4 of 11 attempts for 9 yards when pressured, while Seattle effectively shut down the Cardinals' running game. However, Arizona's offensive situation has changed since then. Minshew brings a different style of play, and the Cardinals are coming off a performance in which they accumulated 467 total yards against Dallas. Seattle will need to rediscover the defensive intensity it displayed in September. Getting pressure without consistently committing extra defenders will be particularly important against Minshew, who showed against Dallas that he can punish defenses when given time to find his receivers. The health of the defensive front is another concern. Leonard Williams left the game against Chicago with a stinger, while Uchenna Nwosu and other defensive contributors are also dealing with injuries. Their availability could have a significant impact on Seattle's ability to control the line of scrimmage. The biggest question: Drew Lock For Seattle, the biggest storyline heading into Sunday is undoubtedly the quarterback position. Sam Darnold will miss the game after suffering a quadriceps injury against Chicago. Head coach Mike Macdonald also revealed that Darnold played through a cracked rib suffered early in that game. He will not be placed on injured reserve, but his return will depend on his recovery. Drew Lock is expected to start, although he has been dealing with an elbow injury that limited his participation over the previous two weeks. Seattle is also preparing Jalen Milroe to serve as the backup. There is some reason for optimism. Lock already faced Arizona in Week 2, when he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-7 victory. He demonstrated that he can take advantage of opportunities against this defense, particularly when connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba downfield. Still, the circumstances are different. Lock will be coming off an injury of his own, and Seattle's offense has struggled to find consistency in recent weeks. The offensive line also needs to provide better protection, especially against an Arizona defense featuring Josh Sweat and Budda Baker. If Lock is unable to play effectively, the Seahawks could be forced to lean more heavily on their running game and short passing concepts. That makes establishing the ground attack early even more important. Final Thoughts This is an important opportunity for both teams. Seattle needs to respond after its disappointing loss to Chicago, while Arizona has a chance to build momentum following an impressive comeback against Dallas. The first meeting was a one-sided affair, but the Cardinals are a different team offensively with Minshew under center. Their passing game has a new spark, Allgeier is coming off a tremendous performance, and McBride remains a difficult matchup for any defense. For the Seahawks, the key will be controlling the line of scrimmage, limiting explosive plays and giving Drew Lock a manageable situation. Seattle has already shown that it can dominate this opponent, but doing so again will require a much more complete performance. Playing at Lumen Field should help, but the absence of Darnold makes this a far more intriguing divisional matchup than the first meeting suggested.

The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks and released their first injury report of the week. They had 12 players listed and eight not practicing. The latter number has five that are not injury related, including quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is on the verge of being traded to the Baltimore Ravens . Not on the report are running back Jeremiyah Love and wide receiver Kendrick Bourne, who were placed on injured reserve Tuesday. Right guard Isaiah Adams, who has been on injured reserve since Oct. 10 was back on the field as his 21-day practice window opened. The full details of their Week 9 Wednesday injury report are below. Starters are noted with an asterisk. An NFL analyst doesn't see Sam Darnold's absence as a detriment to the Seattle Seahawks. Darnold will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury, and the defending champions will instead turn to Drew Lock for the Week 9 division showdown. Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci wondered if that switch will actually help Seattle's offense. "I hate to say this: Drew Lock might give the Seahawks a better chance to win at the quarterback position," DiNucci said on CBS Sports' Just Football. Darnold has struggled a year after leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. The 29-year-old has thrown nine interceptions in seven games, with his quarterback rating dipping from 99.1 to 79.5. Meanwhile, Lock led Seattle to a season-opening comeback win off the bench before excelling in a road victory over Arizona. DiNucci suggested that another strong showing against the NFC West opponent could create a quarterback controversy. "Sam Darnold has not played well this year. For whatever reason, he's turning the ball over. This offense looks stuck in the mud," DiNucci said. "I don't want to say this is a soft benching, but Drew Lock -- when he came in relief Week 1 against the New England Patriots -- led that team back. Played really well. High completion percentage, no turnovers. And then Week 2, followed it up against the same Arizona Cardinals team he's gonna play this [week] with 235 yards and three touchdowns. "I'm very intrigued to see what Drew Lock does this weekend. If he plays like he played the first two weeks of the season. I think this is gonna be a very interesting topic the rest of the season."

This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). away.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai returns to practice, listed as questionable on Sunday vs. Buccaneers
away.blurb: Running back Kyle Monangai on Friday was back at practice for the first time since suffering a thumb and turf toe injury in Week 4. Monangai was a limited participant and is questionable on Sunday night. Head coach Ben Johnson said he's hopeful Monangai will be able to return to action after missing the past four games with a turf toe injury. "Some guys come back a little bit sooner, some guys take a little bit longer. So, you know, those toe injuries, those can be fickle at times, and that's what this one's proved to be," Johnson said. "I'm hoping every week. I'm hoping every day and every week he'll be back out there for us." The Bears will need a strong performance out of their running backs when they go against the second-ranked rush defense in the NFL against the Buccaneers at Soldier Field on Sunday night. "Very well-coached. I would say they play good together. A fast-flowing defense. They've got talent at every level. We've got our work cut out for us again," running back D'Andre Swift said. "Chaos. I think that's what stands out. I think he's always defended the run really well, and whenever you play single high to the rate that he does, it's different than what we've seen earlier this year," Johnson said. "Schematically, it's very challenging to run the ball, and then when you have the talent on the defensive line and in the linebacker crew that they have, you know, those are tough yards to come by." Cornerbacks Malik Muhammad and Tyrique Stevenson also were limited in practice on Friday and are questionable for Sunday's game. Some good news for starting linemen on both sides of the ball, defensive tackle Grady Jarrett and left tackle Theo Benedet are good to go after dealing with groin and shoulder injuries, respectively. Linebacker D'Marco Jackson also is good to go after sitting out Thursday's practice with an ankle injury. Charbonnet is expected to make his return from the PUP list in Week 8, which would be a massive boost to the Seattle backfield. Last season, the former second-round pick had 12 rushing touchdowns, and he’s scored 21 times over the last two seasons. Macdonald said that the team has a “plan” for Charbonnet in Week 8, and while I’d expect him to play limited snaps, he’s likely the team’s best option in the red zone. Is Jadarian Price Playing Tonight? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Bears vs. Seahawks in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Seattle Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price has not played since Week 3 due to a chest injury, but he returned to practice in a full capacity this week and is not listed on the team's final injury report against the Chicago Bears. Jadarian Price (chest) not listed on injury report for Week 8. Seattle still needs to activate Price off of injured reserve for him to be active. ESPN's Adam Schefter shared on Saturday that both Price and Zach Charbonnet are expected to play, so it's possible that Macdonald just didn't want to signal the other roster moves the team is making ahead of Monday's showdown. The Seahawks do not technically need to activate Jadarian Price off of IR until Monday. Mike Macdonald indicated there were some roster items to work through before then. With no injury designation, the expectation is he will be active and play. pic.twitter.com/nfnKI6rBcD This season, Price has played in three games, carrying the ball 28 times for 119 yards (4.3 yards per carry) while adding four catches (on seven targets) for 21 yards. He has not has as big of an impact as Seattle hoped when it took him in the back end of the first round in the 2026 NFL Draft. Still, Price figures to factor into the Seattle backfield rotation along with Charbonnet and Emanuel Wilson. The Seahawks' running game has not been great this season, so it'll be interesting to see what it can do at full strength. There's one player prop that I'm eyeing for the Seahawks' running game in Week 8. home.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
home.blurb: Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team's previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers' Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team's final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday's contest. As dominant as the Vikings defense has been, Bills quarterback Josh Allen presents a unique challenge for Brian Flores' blitz-focused stop unit. Minnesota has yet to face a QB who can move away from pressure, extend plays, and scramble like Allen. The Vikings' QB competition so far has been primarily pocket passers. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills

And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

Both Wentz and Jefferson spoke to the media on Thursday afternoon, with the quarterback having been named the starter for Monday night's showdown with the Buffalo Bills. The move came as Kyler Murray continues to nurse a hamstring injury. Now, one will slide back into the starting role, a role he took on earlier in the season. He has a bit of familiarity with this group, and understands Jefferson's frustrations. He had one goal in mind for the receiver ahead of the Bills matchup. "Just get him the rock. It's clear that the two have a special connection on the field, and that has translated into some big moments. Take the season opener against the Green Bay Packers as an example. Wentz stepped in following a first-quarter concussion to Kyler Murray. He was able to make the most of his time, as he threw two touchdown passes to Jefferson. They were 39- and 22-yard catches, respectively. It was clear that those two had chemistry from the beginning. He has gone 28-of-44, throwing for 278 yards and two touchdowns. Wentz has also carried the ball 10 times for 53 yards. He has played against Buffalo with both the Philadelphia Eagles and the Indianapolis Colts . In his first game against the Bills, he led the Eagles to a victory on October 27, 2019. He went 18-of-24 on the day, throwing for 172 yards and a touchdown. The playmaker also added 35 rushing yards in what was a 31-13 victory on the road. It was a decisive victory in a difficult place to play. His second contest went equally well. This time, he played for the Indianapolis Colts. He went 11-of-20, throwing for 106 yards and one touchdown. The quarterback didn't need to do too much in this one, as Jonathan Taylor scored five touchdowns in the game. Instead, the veteran showed his trademark efficiency as he was able to pick up the victory. The Goal Is Clear For Justin Jefferson And Vikings It's clear that he wants to get football to Jefferson, and that will be the top priority for Monday's showdown. Jefferson will need to have a productive game against the Bills, as the latter is one of the most productive teams in the NFL . This could be a statement game for the Vikings. Although they sit with only one loss on the season, beating the Bills would be a step in the right direction to prove that they are contenders, and not pretenders. Sports Illustrated spoke to oddsmakers about the injury a,d BetMGM's Christian Cipollini, a Senior Trading Manager, explained that the spread would move quite a bit if Wentz gets the start. For now, bettors and fans have to wait and see if Murray is able to log at least a limited session in Thursday's practice. Based on the latest odds movement, he seems to be 50/50 for Monday's showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills. Earlier this week, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and that he'd be re-evaluated this week. Murray and the Vikings don't play until Monday night in Week 9, so they have yet to release a practice report since their first official session will come on Thursday. home.headline: Vikings make bold QB change for MNF with Kyler Murray sidelined by hamstring injury
home.blurb: The Vikings are 6-1 after losing 19-15 to the Detroit Lions in Week 8. Murray finished that game with 210 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception, but his hamstring issue now keeps him out of a matchup against another 6-1 team. During the 2026 season, Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray has recorded 1,022 passing yards and five touchdowns across six games. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz has posted 276 passing yards and three touchdowns with a 106.4 passer rating over two appearances. Kyler Murray’s hamstring injury has forced the team to make a major roster adjustment. To maintain offensive consistency, the Minnesota Vikings plan to start Carson Wentz as their primary quarterback against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. Minnesota Vikings QB Carson Wentz to start against Buffalo Bills “When healthy, Wentz has thrived in Kevin O’Connell’s offense,” Ian Rapoport reported . “Now, a shot at 1 of the NFL’s best.” Head coach Kevin O’Connell said Murray has a hamstring strain and will be considered week to week. The Vikings decided not to risk worsening the injury because Murray’s movement skills are central to his game. Wentz has already helped Minnesota win twice this season. He replaced Murray in the opener after the quarterback entered concussion protocol, then started the following week against Chicago. The Vikings won both games, and Wentz completed 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions. The veteran quarterback has also spent time in O’Connell’s system. That familiarity matters in a short preparation week because Wentz can run the existing offense without forcing the coaching staff to build a new approach around him. Minnesota’s defense will carry a large share of the responsibility. The unit ranks first in the NFL in points allowed at 13.3 per game and second in yards allowed. It also blitzes on 73.1 percent of opponent dropbacks, the league’s highest rate, and has produced a 45.8 percent pressure rate. The offense has been less reliable. The Vikings rank 29th in total yards, 31st in passing, and 27th in scoring at 20 points per game. Wentz will need to protect the football and keep drives alive against Buffalo’s defense. Minnesota’s official quarterback update confirmed that Max Brosmer will serve as Wentz’s backup. An updated team injury report noted that the strain will directly limit Murray’s mobility. The Bills present a difficult test for Minnesota’s offense, placing greater emphasis on efficient play-calling and defensive control. home.headline: Vikings-Bills First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday.
